newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-PROFILE OF WOMEN'S GIANT SLALOM WINNER.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-PROFILE OF WOMEN'S GIANT SLALOM WINNER.

text.p: The following is a profile of the winner of the women's giant slalom at the Alpine skiing world championships on Sunday:
World Cup wins: 11. Giant slaloms - Zwiesel I+II (97), Cortina (97), Narvik (96), Haus (95), Morzine (94), Veysonnaz (93), Tignes (93), Slalom - Semmering (96), Super-G - Morzine (92), Morzine (93)

Other facts: Twice Olympic champion. Won gold in giant slalom at 1994 Olympics in Lillehammer and in the super-G at Albertville in 1992. Won giant slalom world championship title last year in Sierra Nevada, Spain. First Italian skier to successfully defend a world championship title. Five world championship and Olympic golds tie her with compatriot Alberto Tomba. Career disrupted by injuries and illness. Nearly died in 1990 of intestinal blockage while home recovering from knee operation. After winning gold in Albertville sustained career-threatening knee injury crossing finish line in giant slalom.
